definition: Ego identity is a person’s developing sense of self, discussed here as an aspect of adolescent development that can be more or less favorably formed. In this source, its development is linked to parenting style, with emotional warmth relating to more favorable ego identity status and rejection, overprotection, and overcompetitive attitudes relating to poorer development.

reasons: The packet does not define ego identity as a “developing sense of self,” so that core definitional claim is unsupported.

The source supports associations between parental rearing styles and adolescents’ ego identity development, but the definition adds a broader characterization of ego identity status as “more or less favorably formed” that is not established as a general definition in the packet.

The definition claims that “ego identity” is a “person’s developing sense of self,” but the provided packet does not define ego identity in those terms (it only discusses ego identity status acquisition and measurement via scales).

The definition also implies that the listed parenting factors relate to “more or less favorably formed” ego identity development overall; while the packet reports associations/predictions for ego identity status (e.g., emotional warmth predicting more favorable ego identity status), it does not support the broader wording that ego identity is “more or less favorably formed” in the sense used in the definition.
